__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus data source scraping the llm-redact proxy

panels.title: End-to-end request duration incl. the provider (p50 / p95)
panels.description: llm_redact_request_duration_seconds: from admission until the answer is handed to the server (a stream: its last chunk), so it INCLUDES the provider's own time (and a stream's whole length). Not a proxy-health signal: the Proxy overhead panel is the proxy's own share.

panels.title: Warnings by type (VALUE FORWARDED UPSTREAM)
panels.description: Warn mode counts the detection but sends the real value upstream. A non-zero line means values are leaving the box by design — confirm it is intended.

panels.title: Compaction forks (1h)
panels.description: Per-conversation history compaction forks a fresh vault session (documented never-wrong-value tradeoff, docs/compaction-relink.md).

panels.title: Binary uploads forwarded UNSCANNED by provider
panels.description: Binary file parts of uploads (PDF, images, archives) sent with the client's own key under [detection] binary_uploads = "forward" (the default). Their contents leave the box unread; set binary_uploads = "refuse" to refuse them instead.

panels.title: Proxy overhead (p50 / p95)
panels.description: llm_redact_proxy_overhead_seconds: the proxy's OWN time per HTTP request, the request duration minus the waits on the upstream (sending, the answer's headers and body, each streamed chunk) and on the client (its body, a stream's consumer). Redaction, rehydration, vault and audit writes and an upload inspection are included. The LlmRedactHighProxyOverheadP95 alert reads it.

panels.title: Local refusals by kind (the proxy's own answers)
panels.description: llm_redact_local_refusals_total: responses the proxy generated ITSELF instead of forwarding (a block, a body it cannot scan, an origin or access refusal, a vault or audit fault). The provider's own answers are never counted here; the Error responses panel mixes both.

panels.title: Vault map writes queued
panels.description: llm_redact_map_write_queue_depth: durable vault map writes (Responses chains, stored-object owners, Live resumption handles) queued or in flight on the background writer. A depth that keeps growing means the vault database is slower than the traffic.

panels.title: Answers sent before their map writes landed
panels.description: llm_redact_map_write_wait_timeouts_total ([vault] map_writes = "before_answer"): bound = the wait reached map_write_wait_seconds; stuck = not waited for, the writer is stuck behind an earlier write. Another replica may read the record as unknown a little longer (refused or sealed, never a wrong value).

panels.title: NER strings by backend and outcome
panels.description: llm_redact_ner_strings_total: strings handed to each NER backend ([detection.ner]), one outcome each: scanned_whole (read in one model call), scanned_windowed (read in overlapping windows), skipped_max_chars (longer than max_chars: the model never read it, the regex rules still did). Restarts from zero when a reload rebuilds the detectors. Samples only while [detection.ner] is enabled: without it this row shows No data.

panels.title: NER strings SKIPPED (longer than max_chars) by backend
panels.description: Strings no NER model read because they are longer than [detection.ner] max_chars (llm_redact_ner_strings_total with outcome skipped_max_chars): names and other contextual values in them were not looked for (the regex rules still scanned them). The LlmRedactNerSkippingLongStrings alert reads it; raise max_chars if long strings hold names (each model window costs time; docs/troubleshooting.md), or accept the gap.

panels.title: NER strings run inline (not prefetched) by backend
panels.description: Where the NER models ran. inline = llm_redact_ner_inline_calls_total: strings an NER backend was run on by the redaction itself instead of ahead of it on the NER worker thread (the NER prefetch, docs/how-it-works.md), every call attempted, whether it returned or raised. On a request's path that is the event loop: every other request on the proxy waited for that string's inference. A redaction preview in the llm-redact-pro dashboard runs the live detectors this way too and is counted here: on a worker thread of its own in llm-redact-pro releases after 0.17.1, on the event loop in 0.17.1 and earlier. prefetch misses = llm_redact_ner_prefetch_misses_total: strings a request's redaction did not find among the results its prefetch computed (a reload replaced the detectors while the request waited; otherwise a string the prefetch failed to collect), each then run inline and so also counted as inline. Both stay at zero while every request is prefetched and nobody runs a preview; a sustained inline rate held requests up (the Proxy health row's overhead panel shows what it cost).

panels.title: NER windows by backend
panels.description: llm_redact_ner_windows_total: the windows long strings were read in (model calls for the windowed strings). truncated = llm_redact_ner_windows_truncated_total: windows holding one word longer than the model's encoder reads, which it may read only in part.

panels.title: NER entities dropped by backend
panels.description: Model entities never redacted. labels = their type cannot be a placeholder type (llm_redact_ner_labels_dropped_total; usually an [detection.ner] entities entry that cannot be one) and offsets = the scanned string does not contain their span (llm_redact_ner_offsets_dropped_total): both should stay at zero. ungrounded = values the llm backend's model server returned that do not occur in the text it read (invented or mangled), that are shorter than two characters, or that hold a placeholder's guillemet; a placeholder of an earlier turn that a request carries (a compacted history, a pasted answer) counts here too, so ungrounded can rise without the server inventing anything (llm_redact_ner_ungrounded_total; the llm backend only, every other backend reports zero).

panels.title: NER model server failures and circuit breaker (the llm backend)
panels.description: The llm NER backend's model server ([detection.ner.llm]); every other backend reports zero. Orange, server errors = llm_redact_ner_errors_total: strings the server failed on (a timeout, an error status, a connection fault, an answer the backend could not read), what the LlmRedactNerServerFailing alert reads: with on_error = "block" each such request was refused 503 (local refusal kind detector_unavailable), nothing forwarded; with "skip" it was forwarded without the backend's findings. Yellow, breaker short-circuited = llm_redact_ner_breaker_short_circuits_total: strings its open circuit breaker failed at once without asking the server (also counted in the errors). Red, breaker opens = llm_redact_ner_breaker_opens_total: times the breaker opened because the server was down (breaker_failures timeouts, transport faults or HTTP 5xx answers in a row; a failed probe opens it again).

panels.title: Scan captures delivered to the sinks
panels.description: llm_redact_scan_captures_delivered_total: captures of the strings a request's redaction scanned that a plugin's scan sink took, one for each sink a capture reached and that returned without a fault (a sink's fault counts as llm_redact_bookkeeping_errors_total{stage="scan_sink"} instead). A sink receives the UNREDACTED text. Samples only while a plugin registers a scan sink (none in the Free core): without one this row shows No data.

panels.title: Scan captures DROPPED by reason (the plugin misses their text)
panels.description: llm_redact_scan_captures_dropped_total: captures never handed to the sinks. Orange, the reasons the LlmRedactScanCapturesDropped alert reads: the first queue bound the capture would pass — captures (256 waiting), characters (16 Mi), items (256 Ki strings plus detections) — so the sinks do not keep up with the traffic. Grey, shutdown: still queued when a process's 5 s shutdown drain ended, a last drain and never a trend. Requests are unaffected either way: only the plugin that registered the sinks misses their text. Samples only while a plugin registers a scan sink (none in the Free core).

panels.title: Scan capture queue depth
panels.description: llm_redact_scan_capture_queue_depth: captures queued for the scan sinks or in flight on their worker thread. The queue holds at most 256 captures, 16 Mi characters and 256 Ki strings plus detections: a depth that keeps climbing toward 256 means the sinks do not keep up (large captures can reach the characters or items bound at a lower depth — the drops panel names the bound). Samples only while a plugin registers a scan sink (none in the Free core).
